# E0304: overlapping impls

A type has at most one impl of each trait, so a call always means one thing. Delete one of the impls, or merge them.

- Rule: [`traits.coherence`](../../reference/11-traits.md#traits.coherence)
- Reported at: the later impl's `impl` keyword.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `items` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0304:11
trait Named {
  fn name(self) -> str
}

type Thing = {}

impl Named for Thing {
  fn name(self) -> str { "a" }
}

impl Named for Thing {
  fn name(self) -> str { "b" }
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
trait Named {
  fn name(self) -> str
}

type Thing = {}

impl Named for Thing {
  fn name(self) -> str { "a" }
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0304_overlapping_impls.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0304_overlapping_impls.lt):

```text
── OVERLAPPING IMPLS ────────────────── E0304_overlapping_impls.lt:11:1  [E0304]

`Thing` already has an impl of `Named`:

  11 │ impl Named for Thing {
     │ ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

A type has at most one impl of each trait, so a call always means one thing.
Delete one of the impls, or merge them.
```
